description: Add a lightweight, dismissible first-run onboarding hint that tells the player what to do first (train toward the rookie/成長期 stage), enriched with a concise call-to-action derived from the shared evolutionProgress (remaining training count and/or remaining minutes). Show it only when the `ddm.onboarded` localStorage flag is not set; dismissing sets the flag so it never shows again. Mirror the understated EvolutionBanner pattern (no heavy modal). JA/EN parity for all new strings. All storage access guarded so it never throws; the show/hide decision + flag read/write + the evolve call-to-action text live in a pure, unit-tested helper, with the React wiring in App.tsx consuming it. Frontend-only; ships via frontend redeploy.
steps: In packages/frontend/src/ui-helpers.ts add a guarded localStorage layer for the onboarding flag, mirroring readStoredLang/writeStoredLang in i18n.ts: export const ONBOARDED_STORAGE_KEY = "ddm.onboarded"; export function readOnboarded(): boolean (try/catch; returns false when localStorage is undefined/blocked OR the key is absent, true when the key is present with a truthy stored value e.g. "1"); export function writeOnboarded(): void that sets the key to "1" (try/catch, never throws).

In ui-helpers.ts add a PURE show/hide decision helper decoupled from storage so it is unit-testable without a DOM: export function shouldShowOnboarding(onboarded: boolean, hasMonster: boolean): boolean returning `!onboarded && hasMonster` (do not show until a monster is loaded; hide once the flag is set). Document the chosen semantics in a JSDoc comment: unset flag OR unavailable storage both default readOnboarded() to false, and the hint is only shown while a monster exists.

In ui-helpers.ts add a PURE call-to-action helper derived from the shared EvolutionProgress type (import type { EvolutionProgress } from "@ddm/shared"): export function onboardingCta(prog: EvolutionProgress, lang: Lang): string. When prog.isFinalStage, return a concise 'already fully grown' style line. Otherwise summarize what remains to evolve next: remaining training = Math.max(0, (prog.trainingRequired ?? 0) - prog.trainingCurrent); remaining minutes derived from Math.max(0, (prog.requiredMs ?? 0) - prog.elapsedMs) using the existing formatMinutes(ms, lang) helper. Phrase it as a short call to action naming the next stage (prog.nextLabelJa / prog.nextLabelEn) and the 『トレーニング』 action. Keep it ONE concise sentence per language. Build the final visible string in the helper (or return structured parts) so it is directly assertable in tests; use t() message templates for the fixed wording and interpolate the numbers/labels.

In packages/frontend/src/i18n.ts add new message keys to BOTH JA_MESSAGES and EN_MESSAGES (EN is typed Record<MessageKey,string>, so both are mandatory or tsc fails). Suggested keys: "onboarding.title" (e.g. JA "はじめかた" / EN "Getting started"), "onboarding.body" (the primary hint, e.g. JA "まずは『トレーニング』で成長期を目指そう！" / EN "Start with Training to aim for the Rookie stage!"), "onboarding.dismiss" (JA "閉じる" / EN "Close"), and template keys for the CTA used by onboardingCta, e.g. "onboarding.cta" with {stage}/{count}/{minutes} placeholders (JA e.g. "{stage}まで あと トレーニング{count}回・{minutes}" / EN e.g. "To reach {stage}: {count} more training, {minutes}") and a final-stage variant "onboarding.ctaFinal" (JA "もう完全に育ちきっているよ！" / EN "It's already fully grown!"). Keep wording understated and consistent with existing tone. Choose exact wording that reads naturally; ensure JA/EN say the same thing. Do NOT alter any existing key's JA value (byte-identical).

Create packages/frontend/src/components/OnboardingHint.tsx mirroring EvolutionBanner.tsx: a functional component taking props { prog: EvolutionProgress; onDismiss: () => void }, using useI18n() for lang + t(), rendering an unobtrusive banner (role="status") with the title, the onboarding.body hint, the onboardingCta(prog, lang) call-to-action line, and a close button (type="button", aria-label from onboarding.dismiss) that calls onDismiss. Keep the markup light; no modal overlay/backdrop. Follow the project's import style (".ts"/".tsx" extensions).

Wire into packages/frontend/src/App.tsx: add state `const [onboarded, setOnboarded] = useState(readOnboarded)` (lazy initializer so storage is read once). Add a dismiss handler that calls writeOnboarded() then setOnboarded(true). In the loaded branch (game.monster !== null), compute prog via evolutionProgress(game.monster, Date.now()) (import evolutionProgress from @ddm/shared) and render <OnboardingHint prog={prog} onDismiss={handleDismissOnboarding} /> only when shouldShowOnboarding(onboarded, game.monster !== null) is true. Place it unobtrusively in the stage-area (e.g. above or below the sprite-wrap) or just inside the loaded main, consistent with the understated tone. Import readOnboarded/writeOnboarded/shouldShowOnboarding from ui-helpers.ts.

Add styles to packages/frontend/src/styles.css under a new comment block `/* --- onboarding hint --- */`: an `.onboarding-hint` class in the app's understated palette (softer than the celebratory evolution-banner gradient), a `.onboarding-close` button mirroring `.evo-close`, title/body/cta text styles, and a subtle entrance animation reusing or paralleling @keyframes pop. Wrap any animation in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` to disable it. Do not restyle existing classes.

Add unit tests to packages/frontend/src/game-ui.test.ts for the new PURE helpers (import readOnboarded is DOM-dependent; test the pure pieces): shouldShowOnboarding truth table (unonboarded+hasMonster=true; onboarded=false; no monster=false), and onboardingCta for ja and en covering: a fresh baby (shows remaining training count and minutes, names 成長期/Rookie), a partially-progressed monster (remaining counts clamp to >= 0), and the final stage (returns the ctaFinal wording). Assert exact strings so JA/EN parity and formatting are locked. Keep these tests DOM/React-free. The existing 'MESSAGES.ja and MESSAGES.en have identical key sets' test will also guard key parity.

Run frontend helper tests and confirm all pass (55 baseline + new tests). Run `cd packages/frontend && npm run build` (tsc + vite) and confirm it compiles (this proves JA/EN key parity via the typed EN dict). Run root `npm test` and confirm shared stays at 47.

Commit on branch feat/onboarding-hint with a clear message referencing issue #31 (e.g. `feat(frontend): first-run onboarding hint with evolve call-to-action (#31)`). Keep the i18n/helper change and component/wiring in coherent commit(s); do not push.
acceptance_criteria: A dismissible onboarding hint renders on first load (when ddm.onboarded is unset and a monster is loaded) telling the player to train toward 成長期/Rookie, and includes a concise evolve call-to-action with remaining training count and/or minutes.
Clicking the close/dismiss control hides the hint and sets ddm.onboarded in localStorage so it never shows again on reload.

All localStorage access is guarded (try/catch, typeof localStorage checks) and never throws when storage is unavailable; readOnboarded defaults to false (show) when unset and treats unavailable storage as not-onboarded per documented choice.
The show/hide decision (shouldShowOnboarding) and the evolve CTA (onboardingCta) are pure, DOM/React-free, and unit-tested in game-ui.test.ts with exact JA and EN assertions.
Every new i18n key has BOTH ja and en entries; existing keys' JA values are byte-identical (unchanged).
Any entrance animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
verification: cd packages/frontend && env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --experimental-strip-types --test src/game-ui.test.ts -> all pass (>= 55 + new tests), 0 fail
cd packages/frontend && npm run build -> exits 0 (tsc typecheck proves ja/en key parity, vite build succeeds)
Optional: serve packages/frontend/dist via the Playwright power and confirm the hint shows on a fresh profile and disappears after dismiss + reload
